column4: Everyone here says they're fine. Now you can see their weather.
Except yours.
Rule one. You can see everyone's inner weather.
Rule two. They can't.
Rule three. The only weather you can't see is your own.
And you've had a week. Yours is probably the biggest storm on the island.
Guess how many people down there are having a hard week. Go on.
People consistently underestimate how often others are going through hard times.
Even close friends tended to underestimate how much negative emotion someone was feeling.
So why does everyone look so fine?
People report hiding their bad feelings far more often than their good ones.
Which means the biggest storms are the ones nobody shows.
So you decide to fix everyone's weather.
The one helping everyone has the biggest storm on the island.
You know what fine means now. So you ask one more time. Gently.
How are you, really?
You tell her to ask.
When people ask strangers for help, more people say yes than they expect.
We may think we're more alone in our hard times than we really are.
And for the first time all week, you don't say fine.
On Saturday, the boxes weigh a lot less.

You'll never see anyone's weather. But you can ask how someone's doing, and if they say fine, ask one more time. And if you're the one under the storm, let someone help. More people say yes than you'd expect.
